recipes.name: Easy Indian Butter Chicken
ingredients_raw: 1.5 pounds skinless, boneless chicken breast, cut into bite-sized chunks

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Melt 2 tablespoons butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Stir in onion and garlic; cook until onion caramelizes to a dark brown, about 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, combine cream, tomato sauce, remaining butter, salt, cayenne pepper, and garam masala in a large saucepan over medium-high heat; bring to a simmer.
Simmer, covered, stirring occasionally, about 30 minutes. Stir in caramelized onions.
Toss chicken with vegetable oil until coated. Season with tandoori masala; spread evenly on a baking sheet.
Bake chicken in the preheated oven until no longer pink in the center, about 12 minutes.
Add cooked chicken to sauce; simmer for 5 minutes before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Indian Butter Chicken
raw_recipe.description: This creamy butter chicken recipe combines fragrant spices with simple ingredients like onion, butter, and tomato sauce for a tasty curry dish.

video.description: Recreate the amazing flavors of Indian butter chicken at home. This creamy Indian curry combines garam and tandoori masala with caramelized onions and chicken in a cream, butter, and tomato sauce. You can find the masala spices in most larger grocery stores.

review.reviewBody: I originally submitted this recipe. I've been experimenting and have found a healthier low fat version that's just as delicious: 1/4 butter (instead of 1 cup) and 1 can of evaporated skim milk (instead of cream). Turns out lighter but just as delicious. I've also used white fish, scallops and prawns in place of the chicken sometimes!
Fabulous! The only change we made was to substitute the tandoori marsala with 1 Tbsp. curry powder. We loved it and will serve it to company.

this was amazing and super easy! I also recommend skipping out on the salt, and experimenting with the degree of cayenne pepper based on your spiciness preference. Another good idea is to add in vegetables! (red/green pepper's, carrots, asparagus etc.) it tastes GREAT and it adds a bit of health to the meal! try adding them in about... 10 or 15 minutes b4 the sauce is done, depending how crunchy or soft you want the veggy's! :) hope that helps! good luck! this is an AMAZING dish

I've only made the lighter version (1/4c. butter and 1 can evaporated milk), and it is delicious. I've made a few changes over the years. I leave out the tandoori masala spice and don't bake the chicken separately. Instead I remove the onions from the pan and pan sear boneless skinless chicken thighs in the pan. Then I add the onions back and add all the sauce ingredients to the thighs and let it simmer on low until the thighs are cooked through. This makes it an easy one-pan dish.

I cut down on the butter and cream, it was just too much and didn't seem necessary. I caramelized the onions and garlic in 2 tbsp. of butter and then added 1 1/2 cups cream along with the other ingredients. I didn't remove the onions, I just added everything together. I then added the chicken and cooked it in the sauce instead of on a sheet pan in the oven. Less pans and clean-up! Everything came out nice and was really tasty. I served it over rice.

Stellar! Minimal recipe changes:
-10% cream instead of heavy cream
-pan cooked chicken with no seasoning (didn’t have tandoori)
-used no salt added stewed tomatoes instead of sauce and puréed most of them
-onions and garlic took longer to brown than 15 mins on medium heat
-used one pan for onions/garlic, one pan for chicken, large pot for sauce, another pot to make plain rice side dish
Beyond delicious, first time making, picky son loved it (as did I), and now will find it hard to buy/eat frozen version - have been spoiled with this recipe! Had it again for lunch today. Not an everyday food though - the calorie and fat content is off the charts, but of course that’s why it tastes so incredible! Will make again, will recommend. Also, I never write reviews and created an account just to say thanks to mn!

Excellent! My husband is not normally fan of exotic spices but said this was really good! I served it over jasmine rice. I only used half of the cream and I cooked this in one large pot, so I didn’t use the oil on the chicken. I let the chicken cook in the butter and red sauce and didn’t add the cream until the chicken was cooked through. Then I just let the cream warm up, stirring through the chicken and sauce. Glad we like it because now I have the spices!

Worked out well making this casein-free with dairy-free Greek yogurt alternate and ghee. After browning, I bloomed the spices then added the rest of the sauce ingredients. I used skin-on bone-in chicken quarters (leg with thigh attached) and dry rubbed the tandoori then set it sit for 30 mins, then added more tandoori rub and then baked at 425° for 20 mins skin-side down. Turned chicken over and turned oven down to 375° and baked for another 20 mins. Removed from oven and added to the sauce (along with any crispy pan bits) then followed the recipe from that point forward. Served with rice cooker saffron rice and mustard seed roasted green beans (using some of the rendered chicken fat from the roasting pan).

I made a few changes to this recipe. I used half and half butter and canola oil and cut it back to about 1/2 a cup. Instead of cream I use 0% Greek Yogurt but I add it at THE END. Before I do this I strain off any surface oil. By adding the yogurt at the end there is less risk of it it curdling with the tomatoes. However if it does curdle a good tip to know is simply blend it in a blender until it's smooth. It works perfectly every time. I also 'play' with the spices I just made it with Sharwood's hot madras curry, a generic Garam Marsala, some cumin, cayenne and a bit of Anjo Chili powder. I do cook the onions and garlic separately and add them later. I think it tastes better this way. Instead of cutting the chicken breasts into chunks I coat them (whole) with Garam Marsala and Anjo Chili powder, and put them in a 425 degree hot oven for 30 minutes (for 4 boneless breasts). This way they are really juicy when you cut them up into chunks and fold them into the sauce with the caramelized onions. All in all this is a solid basic recipe with authentic and delicious flavour. Thank you for posting it. It is my family's easy 'go to' butter chicken recipe, and we make it at least once a month.

I have made this dish four times now and I loved it every time! But, like others, had issues with graininess in the sauce. I finally figured out how to avoid it this time around! Bring the sauce up to a simmer SLOWLY (I melted the butter and warmed the tomato sauce before adding the cream). Also, do NOT let it come to a boil, only a gentle simmer! If it boils, the sauce will separate and get that "grainy" or "curdled" look. Even if it does get grainy, it is still delicious! So don't despair, if that happens to you :)

Wonderful recipe! I could not find tandoori masala so used more garam masala and a little red pepper. Turned out great, probably would not use as much cream next time as it was quite runny. For the people that had it curdle, start out with the whole pot full of cream, tomato sauce and onion cold and start out slowly warming until it starts to simmer. Stirring the mixture the entire time. Shouldn’t curdle.

The smell and flavor were fine, to the point my wife said our kitchen was smelling like an Indian restaurant, but the sauce was WAY too runny. Without a starch as a thickening agent, the only way to thicken it is by simmering - covered adds more steam, making it funnier, but a higher heat greatly increases the risk of causing the cream to curdle. I don't think I'll come back to this one.
Have made it twice now and we LOVE IT! Super easy to follow and even tastier.
Excellent result. I stepped up the spice a little with some extra tandoori masala on the chicken and some crushed Aleppo chilis in the sauce. Definitely added to the rotation.
So good! I could eat this every week!
For once my family didn't gag. This recipe is 'fool' proof. Even I couldn't mess it up!
Incredibly salty and lacking any other flavor.
Amazing

I have made this multiple times. My wife and especially my adult daughter absolutely love this dish. Served with Jasmine rice and Cucumber Raita, it represents the flavors of India well. As for me, I am not a professional cook but have some classical training in the culinary arts. But just because you are a professional cook (which if you fry hamburgers for a fast food chain and get a paycheck qualifies as a professional cook) doesn’t mean you have a palate for good food, especially Indian.
My family prefers shredded chicken, so I skip the extra step and just poach some chicken breasts, shred them, and put the tandoori directly on it before mixing into the sauce. It is delicious!
